Cyberpunk 2077 Quest Director Sheds a Tear - The Game Turns 2077 Days Old, and He Recalls CDPR's Path to Redemption
items.summary: Much has changed since the release of the troubled 1.0 version.
items.content:
0 19 August 2026, 13:49 Boris Piletskiy Much has changed since the release of the troubled 1.0 version.

This August, Cyberpunk 2077 celebrates a unique anniversary. 2077 days have passed since its release, and the project's quest director decided to mark this date.

Paweł Sasko addressed the community and once again added tear (of joy) emojis to his message:

My dears, 2077 days have passed since the release of Cyberpunk 2077. Oh, what a journey it has been. I often recall the first announcement, the release, all the excitement as the game's rating slowly climbed with each patch, and that feeling of satisfaction when the [Phantom Liberty] expansion came out. Madness and magic. Источник изображения: Paweł Sasko's X account Upon release, Cyberpunk 2077 received scathing reviews due to numerous technical issues. However, CD Projekt RED did not give up and began releasing patches. By August 2026, the project had garnered "very positive" reviews on Steam — an 86% rating after almost a million user reviews.

Currently, Paweł Sasko holds the position of game director for the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel. The project does not yet have a specific release date, and the developers have not yet revealed details.

CD Projekt RED is also preparing projects for The Witcher: a full-fledged new franchise and an expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.

items.title: ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Officially Expands With a Stylish New Release

items.content:
Keanu Reeves in Cyberpunk 2077 Image via CD Projekt Red By Chris McPherson Published Aug 16, 2026, 8:00 AM EDT Chris is a Senior News Writer for Collider. He can be found in an IMAX screen, with his eyes watering and his ears bleeding for his own pleasure. He joined the news team in 2022 and accidentally fell upwards into a senior position despite his best efforts. For reasons unknown, he enjoys analyzing box office receipts , giant sharks, and has become known as the go-to man for all things Bosch , Mission: Impossible and Christopher Nolan in Collider's news division. Recently, he found himself yeehawing along to the Dutton saga on the Yellowstone Ranch. He is proficient in sarcasm, wit, Photoshop and working unfeasibly long hours. Amongst his passions sit the likes of the history of the Walt Disney Company, the construction of theme parks , steam trains and binge-watching Gilmore Girls with a coffee that is just hot enough to scald him. His obsession with the Apple TV+ series Silo is the subject of mockery within the Senior News channel, where his feelings about Taylor Sheridan 's work are enough to make his fellow writers roll their eyes. Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 4 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There are so very few video game worlds that have a visual identity as instantly recognizable as Cyberpunk 2077 . The world of Night City is just drenched in neon, there are enormous corporations everywhere you turn, and you have to look cool if you want to get ahead — that's how to survive there. The game has also evolved well beyond video games by this point, with projects like Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , not to mention merchandise and numerous collaborations, too. But now, you can look like you're part of the solution in Night City.

Cyberpunk 2077 has officially teamed with GUNNAR for a collection of glasses inspired by the game, including designs based on Dexter DeShawn and Militech. The officially licensed collaboration features GUNNAR’s lens technology designed to reduce digital eye strain while incorporating aesthetics directly inspired by characters and corporations from CD Projekt Red ’s universe.

The Dex glasses are inspired by Dexter DeShawn, the larger-than-life Night City fixer who plays a major role during the opening stretch of Cyberpunk 2077 . The wide frames feature an oversized angular shield-lens design constructed from magnesium aluminum alloy, with Amber, Sun and Amber Max lens options. They’re priced at $125 and come with a collector’s map-print microfiber cleaning cloth and padded sleeve.

Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for.

You took the red pill a long time ago — probably before anyone offered it to you. You're a systems thinker who can't help but notice the seams in things.

The wasteland doesn't reward the clever or the well-connected — it rewards those who are hard to kill and harder to break. That's you.

You'd survive here because you know how to exist in moral grey areas without losing yourself completely.

Arrakis is the most hostile environment in the known universe — and you are precisely the kind of person it rewards.

The galaxy far, far away is vast, loud, and in a constant state of violent political upheaval — and you wouldn't have it any other way.

The second design takes its cues from the heavily armed megacorporation, adopting their black-and-yellow color scheme alongside a tactical shield design. The frames use engineered polymer and are available with Amber or Sun lenses, with GUNNAR saying the design is intended to improve peripheral clarity while reducing digital eye strain and sharpening contrast.

The Militech glasses are priced slightly lower at $99 and include a branded microfiber pouch, cleaning cloth and matte metal case, alongside a 12-month warranty. The frames also block 100% of UV light and feature a G-Shield Plus coating designed to be anti-reflective and smudge resistant. Both designs are already available to order now.

Cyberpunk 2077 is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC. The Cyberpunk 2077 collection is available now via GUNNAR.

items.title: I used DeX to turn my Galaxy S25 Ultra into a lightweight gaming PC — and it actually worked
items.summary: Is it possible to connect recent Samsung flagships to an external display and have a lightweight gaming PC experience? I gave it a go.
items.content:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

0 • Hadlee Simons / Android Authority Follow us on Google Discover Add us as preferred source PC gaming on Android has made major strides since apps like Winlator were launched a few years ago. In fact, you can now play older, somewhat demanding games that you wouldn’t have dreamed of playing on your mobile back in 2021 or 2022.

We’ve also seen two major developments in recent times. The first is that GameNative has become one of the most polished, capable, and popular PC “emulators” on Android. We’ve also seen the rise of custom Turnip GPU drivers for Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite chips. Without these unofficial drivers, devices with Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chips and earlier were considered better for PC games.

Between these developments and my prior experience with PC gaming apps, that got me wondering. Could Samsung’s last two generations of Galaxy flagship phones, powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite family, deliver a lightweight gaming PC experience when plugged into an external monitor? I’m not expecting to play the latest and greatest games, but is this a viable alternative to using my work laptop after hours?

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority I’m using a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra hooked up to an old Jsaux dock, which is typically used for the Steam Deck and similar handheld consoles. I’m also running the GameNative app due to its integrated Steam support. My plan here is to try out various PC games, only really switching between the system GPU driver and the community-driven Turnip drivers. Does switching drivers reveal a big difference in performance and heating?

I started with some lightweight 2D games, and I was able to play games like Baba is You, Mina the Hollower, and Battleblock Theater at smooth speeds regardless of the GPU driver. Temperatures were also very reasonable here. It’s not a clean slate with every lightweight game, as Call of Duty 2 (2005) simply encountered a Steam-related error and refused to boot up regardless of the GPU driver.

I then switched to 3D titles from the late 2000s to early 2010s, and encountered a few pleasant surprises. Crysis actually runs at a good pace at 1080p with low graphics. There is some noticeable judder during firefights, but I played this game on Xbox 360, so I’ve seen worse. It’s not a complete surprise, as colleague Rob Triggs showcased Crysis on the ASUS ROG Phone 9 Pro last year. But it’s still crazy to see Crysis running on a smartphone. Temperatures did hit peaks of around 68 to 70 degrees Celsius, but it didn’t stay in this range, and the phone itself didn’t feel like a furnace.

Tetris Effect is caught in an awkward middle ground. It’s not quite as demanding in theory as older action titles, nor is it exactly a lightweight 2D title. Nevertheless, the Galaxy S25 Ultra delivers smooth performance here regardless of the driver. It did seem like the system driver yielded slightly higher peak temperatures in the 60s, though. Deus Ex: Human Revolution also turned in respectable performance with both system and Turnip drivers. The classic title mostly ran at 60fps, with occasional big dips to the high 30fps range. It’s also worth noting that I experienced some micro-stutter even when it ran at an otherwise smooth frame rate. I also noticed temperatures in the low 60s.

Another notable game during this era is Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain. One major issue with the title is that it takes a long time to initially boot up, to the point that I thought the game had frozen. Loading screens and settings menus also hang for a few seconds here and there. However, I found that playing this game with a Turnip driver yielded fantastic results, as the title never deviated far from its 60fps frame cap. Temperatures do reach the low 70s, though. 2011’s Dishonored also ran really well on the Galaxy S25 Ultra via DeX regardless of the driver, lending more credence to my belief that recent Android flagships can handle older or lightweight PC games just fine.

What about demanding games, though? I installed 2015’s The Witcher 3, which was a tough test for older PCs and consoles at launch. The encouraging news is that performance was generally playable during my brief time with the title. I did find that looking around with the mouse resulted in plenty of judder, making for a somewhat disorienting experience, but I feel like the switch to a 30fps frame cap helped. I also found that sticking with the Turnip driver yielded temperatures that mostly stayed in the high-50s, occasionally hitting 70 degrees. By contrast, the system driver seemed to deliver temperatures around the 60-degree range.

My final test was Cyberpunk 2077. The game already exceeded my low expectations by actually running on the Galaxy S25 Ultra via DeX. However, the frame rate generally stayed in the low teens to around 20fps while using the Turnip driver. It wasn’t quite a slideshow, but it was definitely a slow-motion affair that wouldn’t be playable for most people. This was accompanied by temperatures ranging from 60 to 70 degrees Celsius. Furthermore, the game crashed twice when driving through a specific area. So it’s definitely not a stable affair. This experience is still better than switching to the system driver, as the title crashed before entering gameplay. Furthermore, graphical glitches meant save game text wasn’t visible (e.g., dates and times). Still, it’s freaking Cyberpunk on an Android phone. How crazy is that?

My initial impression of gaming on DeX via the Galaxy S25 Ultra last year was mostly positive, although I complained about the lack of support for bypass charging and ultrawide resolutions. Readers noted at the time that an app needs to be added to the Gaming Hub if you want to run it with bypass charging. Meanwhile, the latter feature requires the Good Lock MultiStar app (thanks, Chaldon Pretorius!). I can indeed report that ultrawide monitors are supported via MultiStar. I’m also annoyed that you can’t use or add apps to the Gaming Hub without a Samsung account. Furthermore, I would’ve still liked the ability to activate bypass charging without adding an app to this hub in the first place.

Samsung also teamed up with Google to rebuild DeX in One UI 8 . This resulted in a host of missing features compared to One UI 7’s DeX, but I also stumbled across a horrible controller-related bug. Using a controller in One UI 8’s DeX was frustrating, as the analog sticks would stop working as soon as the S25 Ultra’s screen turned off. My keyboard and mouse worked just fine, though. Thankfully, Samsung fixed this issue with the One UI 8.5 update. So other Galaxy owners wanting to use DeX for gaming should update to One UI 8.5 if they haven’t already. However, I do worry about people with older Galaxy flagships that are stuck on One UI 8.

Otherwise, I found that DeX handled my wireless keyboard and mouse just fine. This support also opened the door to classic PC games that aren’t compatible with gamepads. So it’s been fun to go back to games like Crysis and other titles without gamepad support.

items.title: The 8 Most Perfect Games Like Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Strategic takedowns, heartbreak, fighting for calm amid the bleakest settings...these are just a few elements these eight games share.
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Rebecca Corgan Published Aug 12, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT Polygon Lists Noir detectives and dystopian bartenders abound.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a game about a lot of things, but isolation and self-discovery are major themes. Image: CD Projekt Red via Polygon Sign in to your Polygon.com account Night City won’t let go of you easily. Nor is Cyberpunk 2077 a game you’ll soon forget. The neon and chrome aesthetic, the pervading corporate rot, and V’s Keanu-Reeves-assisted identity crisis are more than enough to build a dystopia that sticks in your mind. Once you’ve left it, you might even miss it.

If you’re experiencing post- Cyberpunk 2077 blues, you’re in the right place. Its developer, CD Projekt Red , did not invent dystopian neon, and there are many titles out there that either show up in full cyberpunk gear or have a similar feel – including these eight games like Cyberpunk 2077 . Some are closer to Night City than others. All are full of bad systems, worse people, and reasons to keep playing anyway.

Eidos Montreal/Square Enix What you’ll like about it : It’s rife with corporate conspiracies, it grapples with augmentation ethics, and it’s got a body arguing with its owner, too.

In Deus Ex: Mankind Divided , set in the far-off future year 2029, Adam Jensen is thrown into a mission to stop a group of rogue arms dealers from selling weapons and augmentations. Unfortunately, that mission doesn’t end well, thanks to a band of murderous mercenaries in creepy gold masks who crash the deal and turn the whole thing into a firefight.

There’s the Illuminati. There’s also an underground hacker group. And there’s Prague, where you’ll spend your time ducking through subway stations, sneaking into corporate offices, and wondering which conspiracy is actually the conspiracy you need to focus on. You start the game in an abandoned Dubai luxury resort…during a sandstorm. As your character learns that terrorist groups are purposely performing violent acts to keep the human race divided and scared, you’ll need to decide: What, if anything, can Jensen do to keep society together when the augmented terrorists have very different plans?

Image: Ubisoft Toronto/Ubisoft via Polygon What you’ll like about it : Here, you’ve got the control and paranoia, just not the RPG.

Where to play : PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X

A mysterious group, Zero Day, has just framed the resistance hacker syndicate DedSec for lethal bombings in London. DedSec’s got to clear its name, then rebuild itself from the ground up. Unfortunately, London is now in an authoritarian surveillance state, and DedSec is public enemy number one. Time to go talk to your fellow citizens to see if you can free your city.

That concept of nameless citizens banding together to save London defines the game, including character creation: Instead of being Cyberpunk 2077 ’s V, a character with a defined spot in the story, Watch Dogs: Legion casts you as anyone. In both games, you’ll use hacking skills, stealth, and gunplay. But only in Watch Dogs: Legion can you recruit basically anybody on the street, then send your brand-new spy into combat with an invisible spy car.

Image: CD Projekt Red via Polygon What you’ll like about it : It’s got similar no-clean-choices bones, but in a fantasy skin.

Where to play : PC, PS4, PS5, Switch, Xbox One, Xbox Series X

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt ’s main story follows a mutant monster hunter, Geralt of Rivia, as he looks for his daughter, Ciri. She’s on the run because she has powers that the Wild Hunt, a ghostly army, desperately wants. Will Geralt find Ciri before the Wild Hunt does? Luckily, his ex, the sorceress Yennefer, is ready to help…

This clearly is not a genre match for Cyberpunk 2077 , as a medieval fantasy instead of a futuristic dystopia. But both were created by the same developer, CD Projekt Red – and both feature dark stories and complex scheming behind the scenes. Do you prefer traveling by horse or motorcycle? Feel better wielding a firearm or sword? You don’t have to choose. Playing both is a great way to discover that CD Projekt Red considers “good choice” a deeply negotiable concept.

items.content:
Bring gear stats and ripperdoc-specific cyberware back to the RPG's sequel!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A few months after Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty launched alongside v2.0, I stepped into Night City for the very first time . The experience was baffling. If I wasn't puzzling over the different kinds of operating systems and playstyles, I was getting an eyeful of every townie's butt cheeks as they strutted about Watson looking like randomized Sims. I powered through the weirdness and learned to embrace it, going on to complete it three times in less than six months.

Anything I didn't understand was chalked up to being a newbie. The lack of handholding or mechanic explanations confounded me at first, but I reminded myself that I was playing a three-year-old RPG for the first time. Maybe developer CD Projekt Red saw no need to tutorialize it too much for the hordes of returning fans, I wondered?

Only now, on my fifth playthrough, has curiosity finally gotten the better of me. One YouTube rabbit hole later thanks to videos like this , I've been confronted with how incredibly different this game was at launch. Not just in terms of being far more stable and less prone to bugs and crashes these days, but in the evolution of some pretty interesting mechanics and systems that I honestly wish I'd gotten to experience for myself. Cyberpunk 2, take note please.

I bounced off of Cyberpunk 2077 for 2 months when I first played it, and that makes it perfect for Xbox Game Pass

I adore games that let me diva out . I want to be the most dripped-out baddie in the Badlands, so it makes sense that one of my biggest draws into the world of Cyberpunk 2077 was V's impressive wardrobe. I made it my mission from day-one to traverse every nook and cranny of Night City in search of the coolest threads V could lay her chromed-out hands on, and for the most part, I succeeded. One thing I shrugged off on my hunt for sartorial supremacy was the fact that clothing items, much like weapons or cyberware, are color-coded into tier grades. In the end I'd just assumed it was a Night City classist thing; grey tier-one gear was simply the cheap bargain bin stuff I'd start out with, while orange tier 5 pieces might run me a few more eddies in exchange for looking like street punk royalty. It wasn't until I finally took it upon myself to research why clothing items are tiered despite only being cosmetics that I started to feel left out.

Surprise, surprise: the color-coded tier levels on clothing items in Cyberpunk 2077 are a vestige from a time when they did serve a greater purpose. Once upon a time, gear could be crafted out of tiered parts just like quickhacks, weapons, and grenades, granting V different buffs and armor values depending on the tier level. They even had mod slots!

Cyberpunk 2077 has finally made me the corpo baddie of my RPG dreams and I regret everything already Six years later, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners season 2 wraps gaming's greatest comeback story With no combat system, Zero Parades is an RPG all about skill checks and spycraft, and it's more exciting for it

This resulted in some truly, uh, interesting fashion choices as players sought to min-max the hell out of their gear (as you can see from the vintage screenshot above, circa-2021). Transmog didn't exist at all, so it was perfectly acceptable to slink into a stealthy thief gig dressed to the nines in stilettos, a polka dot bra, and a hideous fluorescent beanie.

Suddenly, it all made sense. I feel highly privileged to be playing a version of the game that looks and feels fantastic, but there's something fittingly absurd about mercs cutting about Corpo Plaza like a half-dressed Barbie doll found in a dumpster. Sometimes I feel bad for being the only fashionable person in Night City as it is; how could these commoners possibly compete with Queen V's perfectly coordinated red, black, and gold outfits? But in another life, I, too, was meant to be clad in mesh vests and office slacks. Maybe I'm the weird one for sticking out like a sore thumb after all.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

This is not me championing for CDPR to bring back a transmog-less world in Cyberpunk 2077. I'd sooner zero myself than let Judy see me in stained sneakers. But I do wonder how it would have felt to play the game relying on my gear to actually power me up rather than adding yet more weight and importance to the ever-grindy path of cyberware leveling instead.

It's too easy to be the most chromed out queen this side of the Blackwall, let alone the best-dressed merc.

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.content:
Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes

items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
